summary.headline: Orient Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR27 crores, but gross margin fell to 29% on inflation.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue at INR1,829 crores (+24.3%). EBITDA rose 49.7% YoY to INR57 crores, with margin up 106 bps to 6.5%, helped by Project Sanchay savings of about INR13 crores in the quarter. Gross margin was 29% in Q2 (29.4% in H1) as copper, aluminium, steel, plastics and crude-linked inputs kept rising faster than price increases. Management said gross margin should recover only as inflation slows, and it held a long-run gross margin guidance of about 32% and a double-digit EBITDA margin aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by input cost pressure; H1 29.4%

financial_highlights.value: About INR13 crores in Q2; about INR23 crores in H1

financial_highlights.change: Up from about 16-17 days in FY24 per analyst

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue INR329 crores, +25.7% YoY. Consumer lighting grew double digits; professional lighting grew high single digits; wires more than doubled YoY; switchgear and switches grew high double digits. High-value looms were 66% of loom mix.

segments.name: Electrical Consumer Durables (ECD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR550 crores, +24.9% YoY. Fans grew high double digits and gained share; BLDC grew about 26% YoY and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix; premium fans about 40% of fan mix. Appliances grew double digits led by water heaters and garment care.

guidance_outlook: Long-run gross margin guidance held at about 32%; management said gross margin recovery depends on inflation slowing.
Double-digit EBITDA margin remains the aspiration; management expects margins to trend closer to it within the next four to six quarters, with H2 better than Q2.
Revenue CAGR guidance raised to more than 15% (previously 15%-plus), with H1 growth at 24.3%.
Working capital expected to fall back to about 20 days over the next four to six quarters via channel financing programs.
Project Sanchay expected to exceed last year's full-year savings of about INR70 crores in H2 FY27 as accruals rise.
Hyderabad plant utilisation expected to rise in Q3-Q4 for next-season production; steady-state margin benefit of about 20-30 bps.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad facility at about 40% capacity utilisation on a single shift; mix about 75% PPW and 20-25% ceiling fans, largely TPW facilities.
Hyderabad to start producing models that sell well in South to cut logistics and warehousing costs.
About 80% of PCBs used in BLDC fans are made in Orient's own lighting factories.
Working capital at 34 days, with cash discipline prioritised alongside portfolio investment and distribution expansion.
demand_pricing: Price increases: fans about 9% in Q1, about 3% in Q2 and about 3% in October; appliances about 6% in Q1 and about 3% in Q2; lighting 6-7% in Q1, about 6% in Q2 and about 2% in October; switchgear 7-8% in Q1 and 6% in Q2; wires raised every 2-3 weeks as a fast follower.
Price increases recovered about 80% of inflation in fans, about 90% in appliances, nearly 100% in wires and 80-100% in other categories, per management.
Management said there was no abnormal primary up-stocking from price hikes; Q2 pull was split between September and October with Diwali timing.
Quick commerce about 15% of digital revenue, growing about 100% YoY; e-commerce grew high double digits.

Added about 3,000-4,000 fan outlets within a base of more than 1 lakh direct and indirect distribution points; DTM expanded to Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and into Punjab and Nagpur service.
BLDC ASP index about 1.11 vs industry average of 1, up from 1.04 over six quarters.
B2B is double digit overall; about 25% of lighting business is B2B; B2B growth has been slower than B2C.
Gross margin decline of about 250 bps over two quarters attributed by management to input inflation rather than under-pricing; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Did price hikes cause inventory up-stocking in September, and is there any one-off in growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes since April have not led to abnormal primary up-stocking; Q2 season buying was split between September and October, with no one-off effect.

qa_highlights.question: How big is BLDC as a share of sales and what are the plans to grow it?
qa_highlights.answer: BLDC grew about 26% YoY, consistently for 8 quarters, and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix versus about 17-18% for the industry excluding large BLDC players.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend and how is new product success measured?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 0.8-0.9% of turnover; NPDs are about 30% of fan revenue with a 90%-plus commercialisation success rate, tracked by reach, repeats and third-party market share.

qa_highlights.question: When can operating margin reach double digits, and why is working capital at 34 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to get much closer to double digits in H2 onwards, within four to six quarters, if inflation eases. Receivable days rose due to DTM and new segments; channel financing should bring working capital back to about 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth and pricing trajectory move FY27 growth towards a 15%-plus CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth was 24.3%; management guided to more than 15% CAGR, which is slightly more aggressive than the earlier guidance, with volume growth expected to rise as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 250 bps over two quarters despite price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflation has outpaced price increases, pricing has been passed on ahead of peers, and BLDC ASP indexing improved to 1.11; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also contributed.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to about 32% depends on inflation easing; copper touches new highs about every two weeks and steel moved from about 65 to above 80.
Competitive intensity and unorganised players taking share at the bottom of the pyramid could limit further price pass-through.
Working capital at 34 days versus target of about 20 days; receivables rising with DTM expansion.
Wires expansion is limited to North, East and parts of South; pan-India launch not yet done.
Project Sanchay savings need to step up in H2 to beat FY26 full-year level of about INR70 crores.
Hyderabad plant utilisation at about 40% on single shift.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and growth, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly said inflation has outpaced pricing and gave no firm timeline for double-digit EBITDA or 32% gross margin. Responses on working capital and gross margin drew some pushback and were answered with qualified, forward-looking explanations.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, as we speak, there is no predictability on the inflation.
So, there are gaps to be covered yet, and that's a competitive intensity that's there in each of the categories, and that's what we've always looked at it.
Yes, it's a sharp drop of about 250 basis point, but that's not because we've not passed as much as our competitive intensity allows us to pass.

growth.why: Management raised revenue CAGR guidance to more than 15% (from 15%-plus) after H1 growth of 24.3%, backed by price hikes recovering most inflation, fan share gains, and Project Sanchay savings, with no new capacity added and Hyderabad plant at about 40% single-shift utilisation.
